description_text: The company is seeking to act as a key technology and data partner in a consortium under HORIZON-CL5-2026-01-D5-17, providing advanced methodologies for real-time monitoring, attribution, and quantification of maritime and port-related emissions, tailored to maritime, port, and terminal compliance needs. Leveraging its proprietary AI-driven data fusion platform, the company integrates remote sensing, on-board data, and port activity logs to deliver high-resolution emissions profiling across regulated pollutants at berth, vessel, and terminal levels. The company develops and deploys harmonised, compliant data collection and verification protocols, enabling cross-port comparability and supporting regulatory enforcement and auditing activities. In support of new fuel adoption, the company assesses emissions from zero-carbon and dual-fuel engines, helping to pre-empt potential pollution risks associated with alternative fuels. By contributing to a vessel emissions grading methodology and supporting real-world testing aligned with EU certification goals, the company facilitates transparent compliance tracking. Its secure data infrastructure ensures reliable, tamper-proof reporting for both operational insights and legal traceability. Specifically within this call, the company can contribute to: - Developing real-time, high-resolution methods for monitoring regulated and non-regulated emissions from ships and port operations; - Creating harmonised and compliant data collection and verification protocols to support cross-port comparability and regulatory enforcement; - Attributing emissions at berth, vessel, and terminal levels to enable fair assessment and informed operational decision-making; - Evaluating emissions from zero-carbon and dual-fuel engines and identifying potential risks linked to alternative fuels; - Supporting the development of a vessel emissions grading methodology and contributing to real-world testing aligned with EU certification needs; - Ensuring reliable, legally traceable reporting through secure, tamper-proof data infrastructure. The company seeks to join an existing consortium as a technology and data partner, not as coordinator.

description_text: The company is an SME from Bavaria, Germany and is an independent network agency specializing in strategic partnerships, cultural innovation, and sustainable business models across the creative and technological sectors. The company has excellent working contact to the Technical University of Munich (Department for Digital Systems) to develop a project on innovative token-based insurance for art works and other exhibits such as skultptures and paintings in museums. The project idea of the company addresses one of the major financial barriers for museums worldwide, which is the rapidly increasing cost of  insurance around exhibitions and works of art. These high insurance costs, which are offten not required, when an artwork remains undamaged, restricts further investment in collaboration, loan circulation, and access to cultural assets by the general public. Many uninsured artworks remain hidden or in storage, since the insurance rates are too high for transport to galleries & museums. This innovative insurance system is a game-changer in solving the insurance hurdle. The R&D objective of the project is to design and validate a tokenized / token-based artwork insurance framework that replaces classical insurance premiums with a decentralized risk-sharing pool among all participants. The participating museums that join the system will contribute proportionally via tokens representing their insured value of their artwork. In case of loss or damage, compensation is automatically executed through smart contracts, ensuring transparency, fairness, and efficiency. The approach, which is developed in tandem with the Technical University Munich, combines actuarial science, blockchain governance, and digital asset management to create a collective, cost-efficient insurance model for the cultural sector. The company can offer the following key R&D tasks including: •	Designing proportional contribution algorithms and actuarial models for the token pool; •	Building a prototype of the blockchain-based governance and claims system;. •	Testing smart-contract logic for regulatory compliance and data protection; •	Engaging pilot museums and insurers to simulate cross-institutional risk distribution. The project is supported under national German funding and the SME will actively seek applied research and prototype demonstration upto TRL 6 with the help of grants until 2029. The German SME now seeks European cooperation partners to co-develop the technical components of the block-chain token system,to validate governance models with museums, and finally partners willing to co-finance the next development phase for pilot implementation in 2026–2028. The potential partners include technology developers for token-based insurance, research institutions, museums, and investors interested in art-tech, risk innovation and cultural sustainability.

title: German SME offering an innovative insurance system for art works and museums seeks art-tech SMEs, R&D institutes and investors as partners for european grants and funding in culture & creative industries.

description_text: Green Tribology Solutions (GTS) develops sustainable, high-performance fluids designed to replace petrochemical lubricants in mechanical and thermal systems. These eco-friendly alternatives reduce toxic emissions, lower greenhouse gas (GHG) impacts, and offer superior environmental compatibility without compromising operational efficiency. GTS’s current focus is a biodegradable lubricant tailored for the gearboxes and bearings of wind turbine generators. This product is based on upcycled bio-fluids, including non-toxic blends sourced from waste residue. The formulation prioritizes circular economy principles by repurposing waste oils that would otherwise contribute to pollution, offering a cleaner and more sustainable option for mechanical lubrication. The lubricant is approaching Technology Readiness Level 4, with promising lab results in terms of tribological properties—such as wear resistance, viscosity stability, and thermal behavior. GTS is now seeking collaborative R&D partnerships with SMEs, particularly those developing novel turbines or systems where tribological control is critical. These partners should be working on mechanical components with rotational motion—such as gearboxes, bearings, and seals—that require efficient, long-life lubrication under demanding service conditions. Ideal partners would benefit from co-development opportunities, contributing their technical requirements and testing feedback to help evolve the product toward TRL 5 and 6. GTS aims to co-design application-specific lubricant solutions tailored to real-world operational needs, helping partners lower their carbon footprint, avoid pollutant-based oils, and meet environmental compliance goals. In addition to strong environmental credentials, the lubricant delivers high performance through optimized chemical composition and fine-tuned control of characteristics such as pressure/load bearing limits/wear rate, viscosity, coefficient of friction, water rejection, anti-foaming and corrosion protection. Its upcycled origin eliminates reliance on virgin agricultural inputs, avoiding the land use, water consumption, and GHG emissions associated with first-generation bio-based oils. By focusing on reuse rather than extraction, GTS supports circular manufacturing models aligned with EU sustainability strategies. The development is backed by an active patent application, which has shown strong novelty in prior-art research. Early results indicate a competitive edge in combining upcycled feedstocks with tribological excellence—offering benefits across industries seeking to transition to low-carbon lubrication solutions. As the lubricant advances in readiness, GTS plans to validate performance through simulations and real-world trials in wind energy systems. Potential partners are encouraged to engage in joint testing, helping define durability, temperature stability, and compatibility with various turbine configurations. Funding calls in which we are interested: - Eureka EUROSTARS. - HORIZON-CL5-2026-02-D3-07: Improved reliability and optimised operations and maintenance for wind energy systems. - HORIZON-CL5-2026-02-D3-08: Understand and minimise the environmental impacts of offshore wind energy.

description_text: ECOS SCCL is a cooperative group of 16 cooperative companies based in Barcelona, Catalonia, that offer an alternative to the current socio-economic model, based on the values of the Social and Solidarity Economy. Over the last 15 years, a movement promoting a different way of consuming, saving, working and doing business has emerged and developed strongly in Catalonia as a civil society initiative. One of the commitments of this socio-economic sector in Catalonia is to share resources, particularly workspaces, enabling economies of scale, access to other resources, promoting inter-cooperation dynamics and generating physical benchmarks that highlight and demonstrate the socio-economic alternatives that exist in our territories. ECOS SCCL, as a cooperative hub in the city of Barcelona from 2011 to the present, has been one of the promoters of the Network of Cooperative Hubs and the Social and Solidarity Economy in Catalonia (2021) and the Spanish Network of Cooperative Hubs (2023). With this proposal, we want to strengthen the Cooperative Hub and the Social and Solidarity Economy of the city of Barcelona by seeking inter-cooperative alliances with other European experiences. We are interested in sharing inter-cooperative strategies as a vector for growth, consolidation and generation of cooperative wealth, as governance models. Furthermore, ECOS SCCL's partners have specialised knowledge in a wide range of services and are able to effectively support the eco-social transition of social and solidarity economy organisations and SMEs. For this reason, we have designed a comprehensive Eco-Social Transition Service for this type of organisation. We are interested in exploring inter-cooperative alliances with other European initiatives in the field of eco-social transition for SMEs.

Investment Access & Visibility: Organise five international bootcamps and competitions that bring together local founders and foreign investors, supported by roadshows to Europe's leading hubs and participation in international forums to raise awareness of regional deal flows. Policy & Ecosystem Engagement: Collaborate with public agencies, innovation hubs, and business support organisations to align policies, share best practices on market entry facilitation, and deliver actionable recommendations for regulators to ease cross-border investment. description_text: A Finnish SME is looking for a partner from USA to apply for Innowwide funding call in order to create a Transatlantic Fundraising Matchmaker. The project aims to evaluate whether a digital AI-driven tool that matches European startups with private investors can succeed in the USA. The tool compares each startup's fundraising data—such as funding amount, business stage, technology focus, location and key performance indicators—with the documented preferences of investors. It proposes tailored matches, assembles data rooms, drafts investment documents and sends personalised introductions through a secure system. This approach addresses a well‑known problem: many startups waste time contacting investors who are not interested, while investors must sift through hundreds of proposals to find suitable opportunities. During the six month feasibility project four main tasks will be carried out: First, a US subcontractor will analyse regulations and identify any licences and agreements required to raise capital in USA. Second, it will collect and enrich data on US investors and promising startups, adding local valuation methods and sector classifications to our database. Third, it will adapt our software to support US legal templates and currencies, and we will run a series of fundraising campaigns and one‑to‑one introductions to test the matching process. Fourth, it will evaluate demand and performance, measuring the number of matches, meetings and investments and gathering feedback to refine our product and commercial strategy. By the end of the project it is expect to know whether the service can facilitate transatlantic fundraising, what adaptations are necessary for legal compliance and market fit and what the revenue potential is. The findings will inform decision on a full market launch and a possible follow‑on research and development project to enhance our matching algorithm and ensure fairness across gender and other dimensions. Ultimately, the project seeks to bridge the gap between European innovators and US investors, support more investments into European ventures, job creation and contribute to sustainable economic growth. The Finnish SME is specialised in funding acceleration and investor readiness for technology startups. They combine financial advisory, public grants and private capital expertise, and AI-driven digital tools to help companies secure investments and public funding. The company has extensive experience managing innovation projects across Europe and developing data-based fundraising platforms that streamline investor–startup matching. The company continually invests in R&D and digitalisation, creating scalable services that enhance transparency and efficiency in early-stage investments. This active pursuit of new methods, tools, and market expansion fully aligns with the Innowwide definition of an innovative SME.

The partner will need to carry out a six-month feasibility project in their country and help us assess market, legal, technical, and ecosystem conditions to determine whether we can scale there. Partner tasks expected: Regulatory assessment: Identify what licences, partnerships, or agreements we need to raise capital from North American investors. Data collection: Expand our database by identifying more investors in North America and enriching their profiles based on their investment criteria (e.g. type, geographies, sectors, stages, etc.). Sourcing: Find promising startups in North America for whom we could run fundraising campaigns. And, identify accelerators and brokers who could connect us with high-potential cases. Pilot testing: Run a series of campaigns or 1-on-1 outreach efforts to North American investors on our behalf.

description_text: The company are an engineering technology and energy consultancy founded in 2020, specialising in energy efficiency and immersive technology solutions. The company develops AI-powered optimisation systems, IoT-integrated (Internet of Things) smart infrastructure, and VR-based training environments, helping businesses improve operational efficiency, sustainability, and workplace safety. Technology & solutions on offer: They offer an award-winning intuitive indoor climate controller THERCOM that enhances occupant comfort while optimising energy use. Unlike traditional thermostats, THERCOM lets users express their thermal preference rather than setting specific temperatures, leveraging IoT algorithms to reduce energy consumption by 40%. THERCOM won TeesTech Innovation of the Year 2023 award. It integrates with smart building systems and aligns with sustainability regulations for energy efficiency. Type of cooperation sought: They seek international R&D partnerships with infrared heating or cooling system manufacturers eligible for EUROSTARS funding, to integrate THERCOM into off-the-shelf infrared heating or cooling solutions, enabling intuitive user interaction based on thermal comfort feedback rather than temperature setpoints. The ideal collaboration would involve joint product development, system compatibility validation, and market deployment strategies, ensuring seamless integration and scalability across smart building applications and energy-efficient climate control solutions. Desired outcome & partnership vision: The partnership will develop and test an innovative thermal comfort-based solution for controlling infrared heating or cooling devices. It will also contribute to the long-term vision of establishing sales channels and wide-scale adoption in sustainability-driven markets, providing a competitive advantage through innovative thermal comfort control. Eurostars is a European funding programme supporting R&D-performing SMEs working on market-driven innovation projects with international partners. It offers up to €360,000 in grant funding per UK partner, making it ideal for collaborative technology development like this. They are looking to engage with European companies, research organisations, or technology developers in infrared systems, smart energy, user interface design, or behavioural energy modelling to co-develop this next-generation solution.

description_text: The company is an award-winning UK SME with a strong record in cross-sector innovation, delivering AI and secure data integration for government, defence, health, and smart cities. At the heart of their offer is VOLT, a modular data and AI platform for privacy-preserving, multi-organisational collaboration. VOLT supports real-time analytics, federated learning, zero-trust architectures, and flexible deployment across cloud, edge, and air-gapped environments. Building on VOLT, they developed MAXAD—a maritime situational awareness solution that fuses AIS, radar, and satellite data. Using real-time uncertainty modelling and AI analytics, MAXAD enables dynamic risk assessment and optimal drone tasking. They seek R&D partners to co-develop the system, trial it in operational settings, and contribute maritime security expertise. The 2-year project proposal addresses: Unreliable and Manipulated Data Sources • AIS is widely used for vessel tracking but is vulnerable to spoofing, manipulation, and inaccuracies. • Radar and satellite data are critical but often lack real-time trust assessment, creating blind spots. Siloed Data & Limited Multi-Stakeholder Coordination • Maritime security involves many stakeholders (ports, navies, border agencies, private operators) with disparate systems and data policies. • Current solutions lack a trust-based framework, slowing coordinated risk assessment and response. Inefficient Drone Deployment • Drones are increasingly used, but tasking is often based on fixed patrols rather than dynamic risk. • Existing systems do not optimise drone use across agencies, leading to redundancy and wasted resources. Key R&D areas include: • Dynamic Trust & Uncertainty Modelling: AI methods to assess reliability of diverse, conflicting sources (e.g., spoofed AIS, degraded satellite). • Multi-Source Data Integration: Scalable architecture to combine and cross-validate VTS, maritime surveillance, and defence inputs. • Risk Scoring & Hazard Zone Classification: Algorithms to detect anomalies and map hazards to vessels, environments, and infrastructure. • Decision Support & COA Generation: Real-time recommendations tailored to both civilian and defence contexts. • Multi-Stakeholder Coordination: Secure sharing across ports, coast guards, navies, and agencies with differing trust levels. • Cybersecurity & Resilience: Protection against GNSS jamming, SATCOM vulnerabilities, and adversarial AI attacks via edge AI and federated learning. They are looking for: • Vessel Traffic Service operators to develop requirements and integrate with existing systems. • Maritime organisations, port authorities, coast guards, and agencies (e.g., Frontex partners) to validate scenarios, provide feedback, and host trials. • Government and defence stakeholders for deployment insight and EU/NATO framework alignment. • AI and data science researchers in multi-agent systems, trust modelling, and situational awareness. • Universities and research institutes with expertise in cybersecurity, edge AI, and federated learning. The company would be the coordinator and are looking for collaborators with expertise in marine operations on the following calls: Open topic on efficient border surveillance and maritime security HORIZON-CL3-2025-01-BM-01 Deadline 12th November 2025 EoI deadline 17th October 2025 Digital Ship and Naval Combat Cloud EDF-2025-DA-NAVAL-DSNCC-STEP Deadline 16th October 2025 EoI deadline 3rd October 2025 The company offers an advanced marine situational awareness system and seeks partners for development, validation, and deployment. Operational partners will provide domain insight and testbeds; research partners will add expertise in AI, trust modelling, and secure systems. The project, aligned across call topics, delivers a secure data fusion system using AI to assess threats and recommend actions, reducing operator burden while improving detection.

description_text: A Cambridge-based SME has developed a patented Liquid Air Energy Storage and Regeneration (LAESAR) technology — a zero-carbon cryogenic energy system that stores and releases energy using liquid air. The company was founded to address the urgent need for sustainable, scalable, and efficient energy storage solutions to support the transition to net-zero emissions across multiple sectors. Recognised with the Shell Springboard Regional Award, the company is actively developing applications for grid energy balancing, electric vehicles, and marine propulsion. Its innovation builds on the pioneering work in liquid air energy storage (LAES), such as that of Highview Power, which recently secured £300M from the UK Infrastructure Bank, underscoring the strategic importance of LAES in climate mitigation. The company’s core technology, LAESAR, is currently at TRL 4 and offers: •	Modular and scalable design for both stationary and mobile applications. •	Zero-carbon operation, ideal for integration with renewable energy sources. •	High round-trip efficiency (68%) as demonstrated through thermodynamic modelling by Imperial College London. •	High energy density and rapid response, supporting grid stability and peak load management. Horizon Europe R&D Project Overview The company is preparing a proposal for the Horizon Europe call HORIZON-CL5-2026-02-D3-24 – New CO₂ Capture Technologies, aiming to adapt its cryogenic platform for low-energy, low-impurity CO₂ separation. The project will focus on developing a pilot-scale CO₂ capture system that integrates with energy storage and regeneration, offering a novel approach to industrial decarbonisation. Problem Being Addressed Current CO₂ capture technologies often suffer from high energy consumption, limited scalability, and integration challenges with renewable systems. The project seeks to overcome these barriers by leveraging cryogenic processes to deliver efficient, clean, and scalable CO₂ capture, as a direct air capture (DAC) application in an energy storage and regeneration system. Partnership and Collaboration To deliver this project, the company is going to form a multi-country consortium with: •	Academic and research institutions with expertise in materials science, DAC, and industrial integration. •	Industrial partners with capabilities in manufacturing, deployment, and large-scale energy systems. The envisioned collaboration will enable joint R&D, technology validation, and market access, contributing to EU climate goals and the development of next-generation carbon capture solutions. At this moment, it has formed partnership with Imperial College London and talking to a university in EU. They particularly seek a wind turbine manufacturer to join the consortium. The company welcomes any expression of interest before 17th January 2026.

description_text: Fruk FinTech is a Croatian tech company developing intelligent platforms for agriculture and agri-food sectors. The company aims to create a modular AI-driven system for silo automation, real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance, and pest detection. The proposed project aims to develop an intelligent, AI-powered platform for the automation and optimization of silo-based storage processes in agriculture. This system will combine IoT sensor networks, real-time analytics, and AI/ML models to enable predictive monitoring, autonomous control, and active protection of stored grain and oilseeds. description_text: The client is an organic factory and winery, whose cultivation area is 2.5 hectares (3 old Carignano DOC vineyards in Sardinia (Italy), with vines from 40 to over 100 years old, with native roots that, growing on sandy and sandy-clay soils and an olive grove of about 300 olive trees). Since 2011, the company has been notified as organic. The winery produces wine from its own grapes in its wine cellar, following an artisanal winemaking method, whose processes are mostly manual but also controlled and analysed. The client uses solar energy and water recycling. The production of wines is about 2500-3500 bottles each year, depending on the season. The company produces its grapes and wines by using both traditional and organic techniques, which include: 1) cultivating old vines near to the see, 2) sandy and clay terroirs, 3) transformation of the grapes in the winery located close to the vineyards 4) piede franco ungrafted (natural) roots, 5) spontaneous fermentation 6) blending of the separated young wines coming from the three old vineyards, 7) only a microfiltration, 8) maturation at controlled temperature using energy from solar panels. Piede franco is relevant for the biodiversity and a better adaptation to the changed climate. In the latter half of the 19th century, the rapid spread of phylloxera caused the death of nearly 80% of European vine varieties. European vines began to be grafted onto American rootstocks, which were resistant to phylloxera at the root level. A crucial factor often protecting vines from phylloxera is sandy, clay, or volcanic soils. Sardinia has preserved ungrafted, pre-phylloxera vines. The roots of the vines can penetrate deep into the sand, reaching layers of earth where the pest cannot survive. This natural phenomenon created a sanctuary for ungrafted vines, allowing the region to develop wines with a distinctive and inimitable profile. Ungrafted old vines in Sardinian territory can be a notable case study in the wine world. The peculiarity of its terroir, influenced by the proximity of the Mediterranean Sea, gives Carignano wines unique characteristics, highly appreciated both nationally and internationally. Currently, four local viticulture teachers are available to give the lessons at these Sardinian old vineyards, teach how to became professional viticulture specialized in Piede Franco (own routs), alberello vines growing on sandy soil.

description_text: Established in 1994, this Italian IT company is a micro-enterprise with 4 employees, including 3 computer engineers. It operates in the field of Software Development & Consulting – R&D, delivering complex and innovative projects through the use of cutting-edge Information and Communication Technologies (ICT). The company’s mission is to support Public Administrations (PAs) and Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in the development of software solutions and IT services. The company operates primarily in the Public Sector, Finance, and Telecommunications markets, with a focus on the following areas: Enterprise Knowledge Management; Enterprise Process Management; E-Business; E-Government etc... The company offers a concept, an electronic device designed to perform advanced and automated monitoring and control of emissions from heating systems. It enables continuous oversight of the plant throughout its entire operational window and allows for in-depth analysis of the flue gases produced. The solution has a significant impact on several fronts: it contributes to environmental protection, particularly in terms of air quality; it enhances the safety of heating systems; and it supports the fiscal monitoring responsibilities of local public administrations, which are by definition the competent authorities tasked with governance and supervision. The device can interface with existing heating systems or be natively integrated into newly manufactured units. It aims to redefine the current paradigm of environmental monitoring through a smart-based vision that represents a notable process innovation compared to the conventional approach. Its implementation allows for real-time, continuous monitoring of emissions, ensures compliance with legally permitted thresholds and ranges, and enables the periodic remote transmission of collected data to a central control unit for analysis and regulatory checks. The hardware consists of a scalable external casing, produced using custom 3D-printed molds, which houses the internal technological components. Externally, the device is equipped with a probe connected to the flue pipe, featuring a flexible ring adaptable to various models on the market; a micro-antenna that ensures the periodic radio transmission of data using the free frequency band 169.400-169.475 MHz, which is legally designated for data transmission; and a multifunction digital display. Among its main features, the system includes the digital identification of the heating unit, real-time monitoring of boiler emissions via a combustion analyzer with O₂ and CO sensors (up to 4,000 ppm), a compact flue gas probe (160 mm, Ø 6 mm, Tmax. 500°C), a flexible connection hose, and a fixing cone (e.g., item code 0600 9740). In case of threshold exceedance, the system triggers an alert and automatically sends a notification to the central unit, along with a digital request for technical intervention within 6 hours. A dormant, remotely activated ambient sensor is also included, allowing the detection of nearby statistical environmental values and interaction with the central unit. Communication is supported by an M2M (machine-to-machine) SIM card, enabling automatic data exchange without human intervention. Overall, the system offers a reliable, smart, and scalable solution for emissions monitoring in compliance with current environmental and safety regulations. The company is preparing a project proposal under the 4th Innowwide call for market feasibility projects and is seeking an industrial partner who will act in its own country as the main subcontractor for the market feasibility project, under R&D request.  As indicated in the call, the subcontractor must be legally established in a target country (Africa, the Americas, Asia, or Oceania).

description_text: The LIFE-CHIMERA project addresses one of Europe’s most emission-intensive value chains: lime production. Current processes rely on fossil-fuel calcination and generate unavoidable process CO₂, making the sector hard-to-abate. LIFE-CHIMERA provides an integrated solution combining renewable-powered electrified calcination with permanent CO₂ removal and storage through Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement (OAE). Fossil combustion is eliminated, process emissions are avoided, and residual CO₂ is converted into stable bicarbonate and safely released into the Mediterranean Sea under strict Monitoring, Reporting The LIFE-CHIMERA project addresses one of Europe’s most emission-intensive value chains: lime production. Current processes rely on fossil-fuel calcination and generate unavoidable process CO₂, making the sector hard-to-abate. LIFE-CHIMERA provides an integrated solution combining renewable-powered electrified calcination with permanent CO₂ removal and storage through Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement (OAE). Fossil combustion is eliminated, process emissions are avoided, and residual CO₂ is converted into stable bicarbonate and safely released into the Mediterranean Sea under strict Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) protocols. This dual climate and ecological action not only ensures a net-negative balance under industrial conditions, but also strengthens marine buffering capacity against acidification, indirectly supporting biodiversity and ecosystem resilience. The project will build and operate the first pre-commercial demonstrator (1.5 ktpa Ca(OH)₂) in Augusta, Sicily, integrating Limenet’s newly developed electric calciner with an existing mixing module for CO₂ storage. The Mediterranean, a climate and acidification hotspot, provides an ideal testbed. By coupling deep decarbonisation at source with durable carbon removal, LIFE-CHIMERA creates a scalable, replicable and bankable model for carbon-free lime and beyond (cement, ceramics, refractories). The project will generate robust datasets, improve policy and regulatory acceptance, and deliver immediate climate benefits while laying the foundation for the wider integration of novel CDR technologies within EU climate and environmental frameworks. The LIFE-CHIMERA consortium integrates technological innovation, scientific research, policy expertise, and industrial replication capacity. This balance ensures that the demonstrator not only validates a breakthrough process, but also generates the scientific evidence and regulatory pathways needed for scale-up.

description_text: The Maltese company is the technical lead behind the EuroQCI project co-funded by the European Union under the Digital Europe Programme. Through this project,  the Maltese company has designed and developed a quantum secured testbed network across the Maltese Islands. It has also deployed Malta's first  quantum key distribution link on live telecom fibre,  and run multi-site trials combining commercial QKD devices, optical transport equipment and classical encryption systems. The company's contribution is a vendor-agnostic, standards-aligned software stack for integrating PQC and QKD into networks, combined with operational lessons from PRISM and from international demonstrations with networking and quantum-technology vendors. In those demonstrations, quantum-secured connectivity was established between on-premises data centres and cloud infrastructure using QKD systems, backbone fibre and commercial routing and encryption equipment. Within PRISM, they have also worked with local partners on QKD-assisted links and quantum-secured VPNs. Together, these activities provide a foundation for new research that is ambitious but grounded in what has already been shown to work. They now would like to extend this experience into applied research and demonstration projects in sectors where long-term confidentiality and resilience are critical, especially in the finance and healthcare sectors. Quantum-era threats and “store now, decrypt later” attacks are increasingly recognised, but there is little empirical data on how post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and QKD behave when used on backbone links between data centres or across borders. Thus the objective of the next project is to create collaborative testbeds that generate such data under realistic conditions, using infrastructure contributed by partners. Thus they are seeking financial institutions such as banks, or healthcare institutions to create a quantum-safe backbone testbed connecting at least 2 financial or critical infrastructure sites via one or more telecom operators. Over this testbed, partners would deploy PQC-based protections at suitable layers and, where feasible, overlay QKD to supply additional keying material, then measure how these approaches affect performance, availability, operational effort and the ability to produce evidence for compliance compared with current practice based solely on classical cryptography. Academic partners would help define measurement and analysis methods; financial and regulatory stakeholders would map technical metrics to risk indicators and assurance artefacts that are meaningful for supervisors, auditors and internal governance. Expected outputs include reference architectures for quantum-safe backbones, deployment and operations guidance, and case studies showing where PQC alone is sufficient and where QKD may add measurable value. Depending on the funding call, projects could also include training and outreach activities, using Malta's PRISM network and related demonstrations as visible showcases of quantum communication in operation. All work would build on the company's existing activities rather than on hypothetical future capabilities, so that results can be translated quickly into practical guidance and, where appropriate, commercial offerings.

description_text: The main purpose of this proposal is to obtain the biomechanical properties of cellular structures from acoustic wave data scattered and transmitted from healthy and/or cancerous cells interacting with acoustic waves of a certain frequency or frequency range, and the quantum-based imaging information of the thermal emission information resulting from the vibration movement in cellular structures as a result of this acoustic interaction. Thus, the sensitivity and detail of the data that will be effective in the preliminary diagnosis of healthy cells that have the possibility of turning into cancer will be increased. In the related proposal, as a result of the interaction of cancerous and healthy cells with high-frequency acoustic waves, vibration movement will occur in cellular structures and accordingly thermal (emission in the infrared region) emission will occur at a certain energy/intensity and a certain wavelength. Since this thermal emission is micro-sized and low-intensity, it is planned to obtain characteristic information related to thermal emission, especially with a thermal microscopic imaging system. In addition, due to the very low intensity, i.e. the low number of photons emitted per unit time, it is planned to develop a quantum-based thermal microscopic cancer screening device with the integration of a quantum sensor/detector-based sensor in order to increase detection sensitivity. Here, due to the micro-size of the detection, it is planned to develop an imaging system that can perform original thermal microscopic imaging of thermal emission information. In this way, it is aimed to perceive both physical and geometric optical information of thermal emission in micron size in detail. Due to the low intensity of thermal emission information in microscopic size, it is planned to integrate a quantum-based sensor or detector structure (quantum imaging) to increase the detail and sensitivity of imaging information of healthy and/or cancerous cellular structures.

description_text: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) exhibits profound epigenetic dysregulation that contributes to immune evasion, therapeutic resistance, and clinical heterogeneity. Given the limited predictive power of current immunotherapy biomarkers, this project focuses on integrating DNA methylation profiles with immune-related transcriptomic, radiomic, and clinical data using AI-based multi-omics approaches to improve TNBC stratification, predict immunotherapy response, and identify clinically relevant epigenetic–immune signatures to guide for alternative or intensified treatment options for non-responders while supporting the overall clinical translation of AI-enhanced epigenomic biomarkers into decision-making pathways for TNBC immunotherapy. Note: This project is planned for submission under the TÜBİTAK–DFG Call for Proposals, which funds joint international research and innovation projects within the scope of the bilateral agreement between the Scientific and Technological Research Council of Türkiye (TÜBİTAK) and the German Research Foundation (DFG). description_text: COMPANY DESCRIPTION The company’s objective is to enhance the efficiency of municipal and industrial wastewater treatment plants. Hence it is confronted with various issues related to biological and chemical processes regarding the treatment of wastewater. PROBLEM DESCRIPTION The sedimentation of small suspended or colloidal solid particles (especially organic substances) is an essential process in various stages of wastewater treatment. These particles are bound together to form larger 'flocs'. These 'flocs' settle much faster due to their mass, which makes the process more efficient. Artificial polymer flocculants are used to create these 'flocs'. The consumption of flocculants during the dewatering of digested sludge often varies significantly, as digested sludge contains large amounts of capillary and cell water. Some causes are well-known for this phenomenon, such as the fact that certain microorganisms die during the digestion process, releasing cell wall residues that form colloids, which also bind water, or the re-dissolution of phosphates, which can also bind significant amounts of water. As a result, mechanical dewatering methods (e.g. centrifuges, diverse presses) reach their limitations in effectively processing the sludge. Despite the use of flocculants, a considerable proportion of bound water remains in the sludge, which limits the achievable dry matter content. Precise process control, optimised flocculant dosing, and potentially pre-treatment measures such as the use of dewatering aids or sludge conditioning can help mitigate these challenges. Therefore, the amount of flocculants used should be minimised for cost reasons without negatively influencing the sedimentation process. In fact, a suitable flocculation process ensures that the proportion of bound water can be minimised and the achievable dry matter content can be optimised. This is of interest as a high water content increases the costs for further treatment of the digested sludge (e.g. incineration). STATE OF THE ART Currently, many of the factors limiting the effectiveness of flocculation processes remain unknown. Flocculants do not always work equally well, even though they are used in the same wastewater treatment plant. In addition to the well-known charge changes between summer and winter sludge, there are also significant fluctuations in polymer consumption that occur independently of seasonal variations. The reasons for this are not yet sufficiently understood. Whenever flocculant consumption increases or the dry matter content of the dewatered sludge decreases, immediate action is required. In practice, fresh samples of digested sludge are taken from the wastewater treatment plants and flocculation trials are conducted in the laboratory. The flocculants identified during these trials are subsequently tested in pilot-scale experiments and then used in the wastewater treatment plant for as long as the performance meets the expectations of the plant operator. Once the efficiency of the process decreases, new samples are collected and additional tests are carried out to identify the appropriate flocculants. These tests are both time-consuming and cost-intensive for flocculant suppliers and plant operators alike. The goal is to understand the causes of fluctuations, improve the efficiency of sludge dewatering, reduce resource consumption, and simultaneously minimise operating costs and time required for trials and adjustments. The emphasis should remain on fostering sustainable and innovative development throughout the process. PARTNER SOUGHT The Austrian company is interested in a commercial agreement with technical assistance as well as in joint development projects.

description_text: The company is a Swiss start-up in the materials sector and operates since 2023. It specializes in the synthesis of unique metal-cellulose hybrid fibers. Those can be used for a vast number of applications, one of them being electrical resistance heating. The company focuses on developing their novel heating technology for machine part heating and mobility, and automotive market. In addition, the company is exploring the applicability of their metal-cellulose hybrid fibers in electromagnetic shielding. There, their fibers are compounded with polymers for possible applications in extruded cable shielding jackets or injection molded shielding housings. They could already show the basic manufacturability of their material. Technology and Development: The technology is based on the company’s patent-pending material & synthesis process: natural cellulose fibers are introduced into a wet-chemical synthesis in which metal particles are grown into or onto those fibers. The fibers can stem from any natural source and may be of any length, typically ranging from 0.6 to 2.2 mm mean length. The synthesis takes place in an organic solvent, and the copper source is an organic salt, which is added in powder form. The synthesis allows for tailoring the location and amount of metal particles, therefore also electrical conductivity. For the heating application, those fibers are then further processed into electrically conductive paper and customized with electrodes and packaging to form a heating element, ready for integration. The company has in-house expertise and resources for doing all the mentioned manufacturing in laboratory scale up to 5L volume. In the long run, the company plans to outsource the material synthesis step. Partnership: For the next step in further developing the company’s heating elements, they need to scale the paper manufacturing and customization to pilot plant level. This requires a fiber supply on the kilogram-scale and beyond. In the shielding case, the same holds true. For this scale of synthesis output, the company does not have the infrastructure for, marking the time to start outsourcing their fiber synthesis. The company seeks a partner which is ideally capable of producing the whole range of metal-cellulose fibers. They envision a close collaboration, first starting with an initial pilot phase where the feasibility of further scaling their lab-proven synthesis to a kg-scale  is shown, ensuring product quality and specifications, in the frame of a commercial agreement with technical assistance or R&D collaboration. After successful completion, further scaling steps shall be performed with interest to continue for a longer-term partnership.
technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is seeking a contract manufacturer to outsource the production of its novel material. The ideal partner would offer custom chemical synthesis services on pilot/ commercial scale, while securely handling intellectual property. The material doesn’t require optimization on R&D scale and has been successfully scaled up to 5L in-house. What is still required is the know-how of experienced chemical manufacturers to upscale and produce the material in large volumes. More specifically, the collaboration partner should provide 100L-1000L capacities. The company’s needs include: • For application 1: an output of 200kg per year for 2 years at least. This equals roughly 8 runs of 1000L per year. • For application 2: an output of 30kg until summer 2026. This equals roughly 1 run of 400L. After the completion of the upscaling efforts and the production of the above-mentioned quantities, the company would be interested in a long-term collaboration for commercial production. The production of the metal-cellulose hybrid fibers consists of the wet chemical synthesis and the post processing of the fibers. The multi-addition synthesis involves cellulose fibers, a metal salt in powder form and an organic solvent. The reaction occurs in the range of 140-180°C. The post processing of the fibers involves a washing step with an organic solvent and a size separation method, to remove undesired byproducts. The presence of fibers in the reaction introduces operational and handling challenges. For instance, mixing  in large vessels to ensure successful heat and mass transfer will likely require special consideration. Another technical challenge is the (un)loading of the fibers from the reactor which is conducted manually in house. The product’s quality can be assessed optically, chemically and gravimetrically and could also be done by the company if the partner lacks this equipment. Regarding the cost of the service, the company targets a price at pilot scale production (200 kg/y) on the order of 100 €/kg. The company is aware of the additional costs the initial familiarization and scale-up trials require.
title: Seeking a chemical contract manufacturing partner to scale up and produce at 1000L-scale of metal-cellulose hybrid fibers

description_text: A Swiss luxury jewellery company is developing an innovative additive manufacturing process to produce high-quality 925 sterling silver components using MoldJet technology. The main objective of the request is to establish a robust and industrially viable MoldJet process chain for 925 sterling silver, covering slurry formulation, printing behaviour, debinding strategy, high-temperature sintering profiles, shrinkage control, porosity reduction and surface quality optimisation. Particular attention is given to dimensional accuracy, surface finish and mechanical performance to meet the stringent requirements of the luxury sector. The performance of the final parts will be assessed through density measurements, microstructural analysis, hardness testing and dimensional tolerance verification. Sintering technology and densification: Expertise in high-temperature sintering of silver alloys, including profile optimisation, shrinkage control, grain growth management and atmosphere selection. The objective is to achieve near-full density (> 99%), minimal residual porosity and high dimensional stability while preserving surface quality suitable for direct jewellery applications. Thermal processing and atmosphere control: Know-how in thermal debinding and sintering under controlled furnace atmospheres (hydrogen, nitrogen, vacuum or mixed environments) to prevent oxidation, contamination and surface degradation. Optimised ramp strategies are required to minimise distortion, blistering and collapse of fine features. Dimensional accuracy and surface finish: Competence in shrinkage modelling, distortion prediction and surface roughness optimisation to reach jewellery-grade surface quality without extensive post-processing. The goal is to enable both functional and aesthetic compliance with luxury sector standards. Quality assurance and material validation: Capability to perform and interpret advanced quality analysis including density (Archimedes, pycnometry), porosity, hardness (Vickers), microstructural analysis (SEM) and dimensional tolerance verification. Both destructive and non-destructive testing approaches are of interest to define stable quality windows. Process maturity and intellectual property protection: The partner must operate at a technology readiness level of at least laboratory-tested or demonstrator stage. description_text: The French research institute has extensive expertise in infant electroencephalogram recordings using high-density nets with 128 and 252 electrodes in babies as young as a few months old. This is precisely why the institute is seeking research and development cooperation agreements to overcome these challenges and drive innovation. The primary objective is to further increase spatial sampling by developing a new high-density EEG cap with approximately 280 electrodes , specifically designed for infants and fully compatible with the BEL/EGI EEG acquisition system. In infants, the low conductivity and thickness of the skull strongly reduce the spatial smearing observed in adults, making ultra-high-density EEG particularly informative. Increasing electrode density therefore has a high potential payoff in terms of spatial resolution, source localization, and network analyses in early development. A second major challenge concerns signal quality. While dry electrodes are essential for fast and well-tolerated recordings in young infants, their signal-to-noise ratio is not always optimal, especially for cognitive paradigms requiring fine temporal and spatial precision. description_text: Invasive underwater aquatic plants, such as water crassula and large water primrose, are an increasing problem in the Netherlands. These plants spread rapidly and suffocate native flora and fauna, leading to a significant decline in biodiversity. Additionally, they obstruct water flow in ditches and canals, which can result in flooding. Recreational activities, such as boating and fishing, are also negatively affected as waterways become inaccessible. The traditional approach to managing invasive aquatic plants mainly involves physical removal and maintenance. This is done using mowing boats to cut and remove the plants. In some cases, manual methods, such as pulling out plants by hand, are used by volunteers. Additionally, ditches and canals are dredged more frequently to remove seeds and root fragments. While these methods are effective in the short term, they require repeated efforts and ongoing monitoring to prevent regrowth. Early detection of invasive species is crucial to contain their spread and prevent large-scale damage to ecosystems, water management, and recreation. Identifying these plants in the early stages allows for targeted and cost-effective management measures, saving time and resources. Additionally, it helps prevent invasive species from displacing native flora and fauna or completely obstructing waterways. Early detection in Dutch waters is challenging due to several factors: 1.	Extensive and diverse water system: The Netherlands has a dense network of ditches, canals, lakes, and ponds, making it a massive challenge to monitor all water bodies effectively. 2.	Visual similarity to native species: Many invasive plants closely resemble native aquatic plants, making identification difficult without specialized knowledge or technology. 3.	Rapid spread: Due to water currents, boats, and human activity, invasive species can spread quickly, complicating efforts to locate and contain outbreaks. 4. Plants must be identified while spreading on the bottom / the water "floor" before the plants come to the surface. That is why it needs to work in murky waters. 5	Limited visibility: Many invasive plants grow underwater or in murky conditions, which hinders visual detection.
technical_problem_evidence_text: How can innovative technologies, such as AI, drones, eDNA analysis, or other autonomous systems, contribute to the early and efficient detection and identification of invasive aquatic plants in the diverse and complex waters of the Netherlands? The EDIH invites parties to share their solutions and ideas to help prevent the spread and protect our waterways and biodiversity.
title: Dutch EDIH-NN is looking for technology for autonomous reliable identification of invasive waterplant species and sub speciesin blurry waters (and potentially autonomous eradication).

description_text: Based in the Netherlands, the research institute focuses on neuromorphic computing, a new computing paradigm inspired by the way the brain works. Neuromorphic computing represents a novel approach to both hardware and algorithms, applying principles derived from brain functionality to achieve highly efficient computational systems. The human brain’s efficiency, estimated to be up to 10,000 times greater than current computing systems, arises from several core principles. These characteristics allow for substantial reductions in energy consumption. As an emerging field, neuromorphic computing requires collaboration across various technological layers — from materials and chip design to algorithms and real-world applications — to transition from laboratory concepts to practical use. The research centre is seeking partners who can contribute to this ambition through collaboration in a pre-competitive research setting. Specifically, the institute is interested in working with partners who can provide: •	Specific technologies, such as sensors, low-power electronics, edge computing solutions, or embedded artificial intelligence; •	Practical use cases in sectors such as health, mobility, sensing, or infrastructure, where local, adaptive computing could deliver tangible impact.
